clue.text: Claim as one's own at N Yorkshire 'ealth resort

indicators.note: the word health written without its first letter, the Cockney dropped aitch, tells us to drop the H from the resort's name

parts.note: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire, long known as a health resort

explanation.surface: Someone lays claim to a spa town in North Yorkshire, spoken in a Cockney voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ealth signals dropping the H, as a Cockney would say 'ealth for health, so the North Yorkshire spa town HARROGATE becomes ARROGATE; 'resort' simply completes the description of the town.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrogate something is to seize or assume it without any right, taking it for yourself.

clue.text: Espy Rene moving among the mountains

indicators.note: moving says the letters of the two words shift about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone catches sight of a man called Rene as he travels through the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges ESPY RENE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenees are the mountain range dividing France from Spain.

clue.text: Pursued irregular claim to take over

definitions.note: the definition is the present-tense phrase, while the answer is past tense, a loose fit typical of older puzzles

indicators.note: irregular says the letters of the word before it are put in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: An irregular claim was pursued in an attempt at a takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' rearranges PURSUED. The definition is present tense against a past-tense answer, a looseness the setter allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize a throne or right without authority, wrongly taking power.

clue.text: Some trippers I could see coming from an old country

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker notices some of the day-trippers come from an ancient land.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'see' in the definition, but 'coming from an old country' already means Persian; 'see' just links the hidden run to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Persic is an old word for Persian, belonging to ancient Persia, now Iran.

clue.text: Aphrodite's lover said no surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters of the two words come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: The goddess's beloved shocked everyone by turning her down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges SAID NO.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the beautiful youth Adonis was loved by the goddess of love.

clue.text: Green, being day-old

explanation.surface: A naive person is described as only a day old.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone naive or easily fooled is said to be this; literally a creature one day old was delivered the previous day.

clue.text: Trade bike used during periods of prosperity and depression

parts.note: trade means commerce, business
a bike is a cycle

explanation.surface: A tradesman's delivery bicycle is put to work through boom and bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists use this term for the recurring swing of an economy between boom and slump.

clue.text: The second person is amused having nothing to worry about

parts.note: the second person pronoun is you, so 'the second person is' is you are, contracted to you're
amused means laughing

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson: the second person finds it funny and is carefree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The second person' is the grammatical second person, the pronoun 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial British phrase telling someone they are in a happy position, with success assured.

clue.text: A prop on dry land

parts.note: to shore up is to prop, and a shore is a supporting beam or prop

explanation.surface: A support stands on solid ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the beach or land rather than at sea; off the boat.

clue.text: Is sure no concoction is made from sap

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of the three words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure about a recipe drawn from tree sap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' rearranges IS SURE NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the sticky sap that oozes from trees, and something resinous is made of or full of it.

clue.text: One card-game or an other doesn't start

indicators.note: doesn't start says the first letter of the other game's name is removed

parts.note: another card game is snap

explanation.surface: A choice between two card games, one of which fails to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an other' is a second card game, SNAP; 'doesn't start' drops its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Nap, short for Napoleon, is a trick-taking card game.

clue.text: Attack nave I'd damaged

indicators.note: damaged says the letters of the words are knocked about into another order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to damaging the nave of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges NAVEID.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack a country is to enter it with armed forces.

clue.text: Realised what one could have done at the bank

definitions.text: what one could have done at the bank

explanation.surface: Someone realises what they could have done at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Realised in the sense of turned into money; cashing a cheque is the typical bank transaction.

clue.text: If he got in, it would be for at least the second time

definitions.text: If he got in, it would be for at least the second time

parts.words: If he got in, it would be for at least the second time
parts.note: a Turkish commander's title with the word in added after it makes a word meaning once more

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to get elected for a second time at least.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ottoman title of a commander, with IN put after it, gives AGAIN, 'for at least the second time'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was a military commander or chief officer in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: When Perce uttered slander

parts.note: when means as, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: uttered says the name is spoken, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: Perce, short for Percy, is said the same as purse

explanation.surface: Perce made slanderous remarks when he spoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uttered' sounds out the name Perce, giving PERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse is to cast damaging, false statements on someone's character.

clue.text: Take most of the gown

indicators.note: most of says the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: a gown is a robe

explanation.surface: Someone helps themselves to nearly all of a dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of ROBE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rob is to steal, taking what belongs to someone else.

clue.text: Applaud poor actor in London

definitions.note: the definition is short for a district in London, a noun phrase rather than a preposition

parts.note: to applaud is to clap
a ham is a bad, over-acting performer

explanation.surface: Audiences cheer a bad actor performing in London.
explanation.walkthrough: CLAPHAM is a district of south London; the clue's 'in London' stands for a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapham is a district of south London, famed for its Common and its junction.

clue.text: The French seller of perfume

parts.note: la is French for the, in its feminine form
a vender, a variant spelling of vendor, is a seller

explanation.surface: A French perfume merchant is introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: VENDER is an accepted variant spelling of vendor.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant's fragrant oil is used as a scent, and lavender water is a classic toilet water.

clue.text: Picture parrot, it needed renovation

indicators.note: needing renovation means being rebuilt, so the letters of the two words are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A painting of a parrot had to be restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed renovation' rearranges PARROT IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painting or drawing of a subject, typically a person.

clue.text: Two wines favoured in Lancashire

parts.note: red is one kind of wine
rosé is another kind of wine, pink in colour

explanation.surface: A pair of wines are the preferred drinks in Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: The red rose is the emblem of Lancashire, a county in north-west England, the House of Lancaster's badge in the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: This flower is the heraldic symbol adopted by Lancashire, worn with pride by its people.

clue.text: To grope about is the name of the game

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles around and says that is the name of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrabble is to scratch or feel about with the hands; it is also the trademark name of a board game of word tiles.

clue.text: Place something near something else perform, ing physical exercises with soap!

indicators.note: performing in the sense of putting on a show of tricks, so the letters do acrobatics into another order

parts.note: PE is short for physical education, physical exercises at school

explanation.surface: Someone does a workout with a bar of soap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges PE (physical exercises) with SOAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To appose is to set one thing beside or against another, putting them side by side.

clue.text: Plainly not in a hairy fashion

explanation.surface: Something is stated frankly, or done in a hairless manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak this way is to speak bluntly, without softening; literally it describes acting like someone with no hair.

clue.text: Fierce woman found by artilleryman in port

indicators.note: in says the gunner is placed inside the name of the port

parts.note: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain
RA is the Royal Artillery, so a gunner in it

explanation.surface: A ferocious woman is discovered by a soldier in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, often stands for a gunner in crosswords; Vigo is a Spanish port.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, violent or bad-tempered woman, a termagant.

clue.text: Do you shortly change colour?

indicators.note: shortly says the phrase is clipped, losing a letter as in the contraction d'ye

parts.note: taken as written
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether they will soon be turning a different colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do you' in old dialect is DO YE, clipped by 'shortly' to D'YE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dye cloth or hair is to give it a new tint.

clue.text: It's to do with the shoulder of part of a monastic habit

definitions.text: It's to do with the shoulder

explanation.surface: A garment covering the shoulder is part of a monk's dress.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it relates to the shoulder blade; as a noun it is the long apron-like cloth hanging from a monk's shoulders.

clue.text: And it isn't Richard stopping short of Northern Europe

parts.note: nor means and not, continuing a negative

indicators.note: stopping short says the name ends early, losing its last letter

parts.note: Dick is a familiar form of Richard

explanation.surface: Someone denies that Richard halts before reaching Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping short' cuts DICK to DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic describes Scandinavia, Finland and Iceland and their peoples.

clue.text: Music that's not hard on one's hearing

explanation.surface: Some music is gentle on the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre of soft, undemanding background music; literally, something comfortable to hear.
